entry.title: Incident handling
entry.summary: How the example organisation handles an incident, written once for every product and classified as organisation-wide measures.
entry.content:
Note

This page is an invented example of a TOM classification. It is not legal advice.

The example organisation handles incidents the same way for every product it runs. This page describes that process once. Product pages link here instead of repeating it.

How an incident runs

  1. Whoever notices the problem opens an incident and names an owner.
  2. The owner restores service from the latest backup when data is affected.
  3. Within five working days, the owner writes a short review: what happened, why, and what changes.

Why the classification says organisation

The process does not belong to one system. Its tom_classification entries carry scope: organisation, so a later export can list these measures once, as inherited, for every product that links here.
